metadata.note: VM rehearsal of a REINSTALL that keeps an encrypted data disk — torre-amd's games disk, shrunk. /dev/vda is wiped and installed (encrypted root, same passphrase as the kept disk so the initramfs password cache can open both). /dev/vdb is the KEPT disk: before `dasik apply` runs, scripts/vmtest/pre-preserved-luks.sh builds it inside the live ISO (LUKS2 with the fixed UUID below, btrfs with @ and @snapshots, a marker file, and two fake systemd-fido2 tokens on keyslots 1 and 2) and CLOSES it — exactly the state a real games disk is in on the ISO. What it proves: the install plans no luks_token change for the kept disk (its header is read through /dev/disk/by-uuid while closed and already carries both tokens), the installed fstab names /dev/mapper/games for both subvolumes, and the booted machine unlocks the disk and mounts it with the marker intact. The tokens are fake, so the boot falls back to the passphrase after token-timeout. Packages are the minimum that boots and runs dasik. Public test passphrase 'keptpass'. NOT for real hardware. `nofail` in luks_options makes the kept disk optional: guest-preserved-luks-absent.sh boots the same image with vdb DETACHED and asserts the machine still comes up (no emergency shell), with Games simply not mounted. `nofail` keeps the kept disk OFF the kernel cmdline: the real system unlocks it from crypttab, first from the passphrase/PIN the root unlock left in the kernel keyring, and `timeout=1s` makes any prompt beyond that give up at once instead of waiting on a console nobody watches. (`headless=true` was measured here to refuse even the CACHED passphrase — 'Password querying disabled via headless option' — so it cannot be used for this.) guest-preserved-luks-rekey.sh + guest-preserved-luks-locked.sh change its passphrase and prove that a boot which cannot open it silently (no token, different passphrase) still comes up with no prompt pending.

files.content:
[Service]
# Show what an unlock is doing ON SCREEN, not only in the journal: "Asking
# FIDO2 token", "Please confirm presence on security token", "Security
# token not present ... please plug it in". Without it the console stays
# black while the key is waited for or touched.
Environment=SYSTEMD_LOG_TARGET=console
StandardOutput=journal+console
StandardError=journal+console

# The console drop-in must reach the initramfs, where the root is unlocked.
install_items+=" /etc/systemd/system/systemd-cryptsetup@.service.d/10-console.conf "

[Unit]
# The login screen waits for the games unlock, so its messages are seen on
# the console instead of hidden behind the greeter. nofail + short timeouts
# keep that wait to seconds when the key or the disk is missing.
After=systemd-cryptsetup@games.service

[Unit]
Description=Stand-in display manager: records the games unlock state when it starts

[Service]
Type=oneshot
RemainAfterExit=yes
ExecStart=/bin/sh -c 'systemctl show -p ActiveState --value systemd-cryptsetup@games.service > /run/dm-saw-games'

[Install]
WantedBy=multi-user.target
Alias=display-manager.service
